title: Randomized determinant test for perfect matchings
statement: Let $n,k,m$ be natural numbers, let $A$ be an $n\times n$ Boolean matrix whose bipartite graph has a perfect matching, and let $R$ be a commutative domain. Assume $2n\le 2^k$, the natural-number embedding into $R$ is injective on the integers from $0$ through $2^k-1$, and $n^2k\le m$. Choose a uniformly random bit string of length $m$; divide it into consecutive blocks of $k$ bits and interpret each block as a natural number. Form the matrix that has these values, embedded in $R$, at the positions where $A$ is $1$, and zero elsewhere. The probability that this matrix has nonzero determinant is at least $1/2$.
hypotheses_covered: the bipartite graph represented by $A$ has a perfect matching
natural-number casting into $R$ is injective on the range from $0$ to $2^k-1$
